JUSTICE VINOD KUMAR SINHA ORAL ORDER 3 24-02-2020 Petitioner seeks regular bail in connection with Madhuban P.S. Case No. 131 of 2012 registered for the offence punishable under Sections 147, 148, 149, 302, 307, 504 and 506 of the Indian Penal Code. As per FIR, petitioner is named in the FIR. Considering the submissions of both the parties and in view of the fact that the petitioner was absconding for a long time causing delay in conclusion of the Trial, I am not inclined to grant regular bail at this stage. However, the petitioner shall be at liberty to renew his prayer for bail after framing of the charge. Accordingly, this application is disposed of. uma/- (Vinod Kumar Sinha, J) U T

On the basis of said complaint police registered Khardah Police Station Case No.404 of 2020 dated 9th August, 2020. Mr. Rajdeep Mazumder, learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner has assailed initiation of criminal proceeding on the ground that police authority without following the ratio of Lalita Kumari’s case reported in (2014) 2 SCC 1 without making preliminary inquiry straightway initiated FIR against the petitioner and his family members. The FIR, therefore, cannot withstand and it is liable to be quashed. The Hon’ble Supreme Court in the case of Lalita Kumari (supra) enumerated five categories of cases where the Investigating Authority may initiate preliminary inquiry before starting a specific case. The first category of cases is cases involving matrimonial dispute. In Lalit Kumari it was never stated that initiation of a specific case without preliminary inquiry in a matrimonial dispute should be treated as illegality and abuse of the process of law and accordingly should be quashed. In all fitness of the matter I am of the view that in the instant case the Investigating Authority should hold a preliminary inquiry after giving notice to the petitioner and his family members. During the period of preliminary inquiry the process of investigation by Khardah Police Station Case No.404 of 2020 shall remain stayed. Initiation of investigation will depend upon the result of preliminary inquiry made by the Investigating Officer. 2 With the above order, the instant revision is disposed of on contest, however, without costs.

Rule-5 of Hindu Marriage and Divorce (Orissa High Court) Rules, 1956 has succinctly enunciates as: “5. (b) In every petition under Section 11 of the Act on the ground that the condition in Section 5 (1) is contravened the petition shall make the spouse alleged to be living at the time of the marriage a co- respondent. (c) In every petition under Section 13 (2) (i) of the Act the petition shall make “the other wife” mentioned in that section a co-respondent.” W.P. Questioning the judgment and decree in O.S.No.190 of 2005 on the file of the Principal Junior Civil Judge, Adoni, the petitioner filed A.S.No.44 of 2018 on the file of the II Additional District Judge, Kurnool at Adoni. Along with the appeal, he filed I.A.No.423 of 2018 seeking stay of execution of the decree and judgment in O.S.No.190 of 2005. Being aggrieved by the order passed in I.A.No.423 of 2018 in A.S.No.44 of 2018 refusing to order for suspension of the operation of the judgment in O.S.No.190 of 2005, the present revision petition is filed. The revision petitioner is the appellant in A.S.No.44 of 2018. The petitioner’s grievance is that the lower appellate court, without considering the Lok Adalat Award, dated 20.03.1997, which was marked as Ex.B1, where a direction was given to the petitioner to pay maintenance to the respondents till attaining the age of majority, dismissed the I.A.No.423 of 2018 filed by him seeking stay of execution of the decree and judgment in O.S.No.190 of 2005 passed by the trial court, without proper appreciation of the material on record wherefrom it is clear that issue relating to payment of maintenance was settled between the parties before Lok Adalat, and in the award passed by the Lok Adalat the petitioner was directed to pay maintenance to the respondents till JUD,J CRP.No.2209 of 2019 2 attaining the age of majority, and that they became majors and employed well. The petitioner’s further contention is that the respondents having entered into compromise before the Lok Adalat, they are estopped from disputing the Lok Adalat award. Having regard to the questions of facts raised in the grounds of appeal, which need to be examined and answered after hearing of the appeal finally, I deem it appropriate to order for suspension of the operation of the judgment and decree passed in O.S.No.190 of 2005, on the file of the Principal Junior Civil Judge, Adoni, which relief the lower appellate court refused to grant, to protect the interests of the revision petitioner till final disposal of the appeal by fixing certain period

By the impugned notice the petitioner is directed to submit two documents a) Ownership document duly attested b) Lok Ayukta clearance order. This Writ petition has been filed challenging the request of the Municipal Corporation to secure the clearance from the Lok Ayukta. The learned counsel for the petitioner points out that this is totally contrary to Hyderabad Municipal Corporation Act(for short ‘the Act) as applicable to Visakhapatnam. The learned Standing Counsel after obtaining instructions states that what is pointed out by the learned counsel for the petitioner is correct in so far as it relates to clearance order from the Lok Ayukta. So far as the ownership documents are concerned, he submits that the Act itself requires that the petitioner who applies for a building plan would supply a copy of the title deed duly attested by a Gazetted Officer. Therefore, the learned standing counsel points out that the short fall notice is correct as per law. This Court after hearing both the learned counsel agrees with what is stated by them, but securing the certificate from the Lok Ayukta is not mentioned in the Act as applicable to Visakhapatnam. However, the Act mandates 2 that the applicant, for building plan, should supply the duly attested copies of his title deed. Since the demand is strictly in accordance with law, this Court is of the opinion that the shortfall notice should be partially set aside and the petitioner should be directed to submit his duly attested title deed/deeds online to the respondents. The respondents shall thereafter process in accordance with law and complete the entire exercise within a period of four (4) weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order. The respondents are at liberty to decide the issue in accordance with law uninfluenced by the fact that an order has been passed by this Court. With these observations, the Writ petition is disposed of. There shall be no order as to costs. Miscellaneous petitions pending if any, shall stand closed. _________________________________ JUSTICE D.V.S.S.SOMAYAJULU Date: 01.12.2020 TM
